Ex chef here. Cooking pots of rice for for 50+ we had a simple method. Rinse off rice first, either by steeping and draining a few times or leaving under a gentle flow of cold water. Once cooked drop immediately into cold water again. Cool the lot and and stop it cooking any further. You should be left with dry easy to mange rice once strained. Heat as required.

First of all, you want to use a long grain rice. Shorter grain rices have more starch and will be gummier. Rinsing the rice to remove excess starch is definitely recommended. I personally forgo the rinsing process altogether and toast the dry rice in a pan with a little bit of oil before cooking it. I've found that toasting the rice is usually all I need to do to get fluffy, separated rice (probably has more to do with the oil than the toasting, to be honest), but you may want to try both rinsing and toasting for supreme results.

I don't toast the rice until it's golden brown or anything, just until I start to see the colour change. Usually only takes a couple minutes.
